title: Meet Guest360: One Guest, Finally One Profile
summary: Meet Guest360: One Guest, Finally One Profile by PAR Technology . . Click to learn more now.
body_markdown:
Guest360 turns the guest data you already have across POS, payments, loyalty, and online ordering into one profile you can actually act on.


Picture a regular. We’ll call her Evelyn. She orders the same iced latte most Tuesdays around lunch. She pays with the same card every time. She’s been a loyalty member for over a year, though she barely opens the app.


To your POS, she’s one guest. To your payments system, she’s another. To your loyalty platform, she’s a third — someone who signed up once and mostly went quiet. Three systems, three partial pictures, and not one of them shows your team the whole person standing at the counter.


This isn’t a data-entry problem. It’s a design problem. Every system you run does exactly what it was built to do — take an order, process a payment, track a punch card — and none of them were built to talk to each other. The guest doesn’t experience your business in silos. Only your systems do.


Guest360 exists to close that gap. It’s PAR’s guest data and activation platform, built to take the information you already have and turn it into one accurate profile per guest. Not a new database to maintain, and not another dashboard to check. It’s the layer that connects the systems you’re already running, so the guest your team recognizes at the counter is the same guest your marketing team can recognize, understand, and reach.


That happens in four moves: recognize, connect, understand, and activate. Here’s what each one means in practice.


### Recognize: One Guest, Not Five Records


Every interaction a guest has with your brand throws off a signal: a card number, an email address, a phone number, a loyalty ID, a timestamped visit. Individually, each looks like a fragment. Run them through five different systems and that same guest can show up as five different guests, never in a room together but connected all the same. Guest360 uses deterministic matching to connect those known interactions back to a single guest, instead of treating each system’s record as its own person.


We’ll walk through exactly how this resolves for one guest — and what changes once your systems stop guessing — in an upcoming post. For now, the short version: recognition isn’t about learning something new about a guest. It’s about refusing to forget what you already know, every time she shows up somewhere else.


### Connect: Turning Signals Into a Unified, Enriched Profile


Once a guest is recognized, resolving the record is only half the job. Guest360 connects those signals into a single, enriched profile: visit patterns, favorite items, preferred channel, loyalty status, how long it’s been since her last visit. The kind of context a good manager would know about a regular by heart, available for every guest, not just the ones your team happens to recognize by face.


That’s the difference between a resolved record and a connected profile. One tells you she exists. The other tells you who she is.


### Understand: See One Guest, or See Them All


A connected profile is only as useful as what it lets you do with it next. Guest360’s analytics show you overall guest behavior across the business, not just one profile at a time. Zoom in and you get the individual view the last section describes; zoom out and segmentation and analytics together show you your guests as a whole.


That’s also where the living segments live — not static export lists, but audiences that update as guest behavior does: the regulars, the guests who’ve gone quiet, the ones who order constantly through the app but have never once been asked to join the loyalty program. That last group matters more than it sounds. A guest who behaves like a member and isn’t one isn’t a low-value guest — she’s an invitation nobody has sent yet. We’ll dig into what these segments actually look like, guest by guest, in a piece built specifically around them.


Layer in PAR Intelligence and you can go a step further than seeing a shift in behavior — you can ask what caused it. Notice a change across a segment and ask PAR Intelligence what drove it, in plain language, instead of digging through a report to find out yourself. Once you have that answer, the next move is obvious: act on it.


### Activate: From Insight to Action, Without Leaving the Platform


Insight that stays in a dashboard doesn’t move revenue. Guest360’s segments live on a shared segmentation service, so you can activate them directly in Punchh, PAR’s loyalty and offers platform, with real campaigns. No exporting an audience to a separate system and hoping the handoff holds up. With PAR Intelligence, you can build segments and campaigns straight from a recommendation, the moment you have one.


And because Guest360 has closed-loop attribution back to the POS, it doesn’t stop at launch. It tells you how the campaign actually performed, so you know what worked without opening a second tool to check.
This is the half of the story a guest data platform alone can’t tell. Guest360 isn’t just where guest data lives. It’s where it goes to work, and where you find out whether that work paid off.


That loop — recognize, connect, understand, activate — is the whole point. Guest360 isn’t four separate features bolted together. It’s one continuous cycle, and it gets smarter about every guest each time it runs.


### See It for Yourself


Guest360 is live starting this week. This post is the first stop, not the whole story. Over the next several weeks, we’ll go deeper on how recognition actually works, what your guest segments really look like, and what it means to activate and prove results without ever leaving the platform. Your guests already trust you with a lot — their card, their number, their regular order. Guest360 is what makes sure your systems trust each other with the same guest, too.
